data.title: Bears will be yelling fire in crowded theater - Dan Ives
data.description:
The AI trade (AIQ) (ARTY) (THNQ) (BOTZ) (CHAT) faces a bumpy road in the coming months as market fears, political pressure and the departure of Nvidia's (NVDA) Jensen Huang embolden technology bears, but the long-term investment thesis remains intact, according to Yorkville Ives analyst and famed tech bull Dan Ives.

"The bears will feel validated after being doubters of the AI Revolution since early 2023 and will be louder and louder over the coming weeks and months," Ives wrote in a post.

"Yelling fire in a crowded theater moment is here and the bears will take center stage,"amid global market uncertainty and a "Blue Tidal Wave" in Washington targeting Big Tech, creating further volatility for technology stocks, he said.

But Ives argued that the underlying demand for AI infrastructure remains too powerful to derail the broader technology transformation.

He pointed to 160 gigawatts of AI-related power demand and backlog through 2029, compared with roughly 80 GW to 100 GW of planned capacity expansion over the next several years.

"This technology wave will continue at high speed and the Blue Wave, bears, China hawks are not stopping this 4th Industrial Revolution," Ives said.

data.title: 'Hunger Games' helps box office rebound amid GTA 6 fever
data.description:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping brought audiences back to Panem in force, opening with an estimated $120M domestically and helping lift the overall box office sharply from the prior weekend.

Lionsgate’s (LION) latest entry in the franchise debuted at No. 1 from 4,018 locations, averaging about $29,866 per theater. The film added $105M internationally for a $225M worldwide opening and generated $26.4M globally from IMAX (IMAX), the biggest IMAX debut in franchise history.

The broader domestic marketplace collected an estimated $168.08M across 39 reported titles, up 89.5% from the prior weekend but down 8.2% from the comparable 2025 frame, when Wicked: For Good opened to $147M. The top 10 accounted for about $158.31M. Domestic box-office revenue for 2026 now stands at $8.97B, up 20.4% from the comparable period last year and roughly $1.03B short of $10B.

For investors tracking theatrical demand through ticket receipts, the weekend offered a notable rebound ahead of Thanksgiving, even with the launch of Take-Two Interactive’s (TTWO) Grand Theft Auto VI competing for consumers’ entertainment time.

Rentrak’s Paul Dergarabedian said speculation that GTA VI would hurt The Hunger Games appeared misplaced, arguing that “both can do just fine.”

Rocky punches into second

Amazon (AMZN) MGM Studios’ I Play Rocky expanded from limited release into 2,477 theaters and collected an estimated $9.33M, good for second place. Its domestic total reached $10.42M. The film also earned an A+ CinemaScore, a rare mark of strong audience approval.

Paramount’s (SKYD) Ebenezer, last weekend’s No. 1 film, slipped to third with $7.7M, down about 60% in its second weekend. Its domestic total reached $32.5M, with another $45.9M internationally.

Warner Bros.’ (SKYD) The Cat in the Hat placed fourth with $6.9M, followed by Godzilla Minus Zero at $2.7M.

The remainder of the top 10 was tightly packed. You Can See Everything and Wild Horse Nine each collected about $2.5M, followed by Sony’s (SONY) Ghost Soldier at $2.4M, Wildwood at $2.3M and Ramayana at $2.1M.

Thanksgiving next

Studios now turn to the five-day Thanksgiving frame, when several new releases will challenge Sunrise on the Reaping. Disney’s (DIS) Hexed and Universal’s (CMCSA) Focker in Law open wide Wednesday, while Neon expands Paper Tiger and Netflix (NFLX) begins an exclusive IMAX run for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Angel Studios’ Hershey opens Thanksgiving Day.

Last year’s five-day Thanksgiving period generated $290.31M domestically. The record remains $424.9M from 2024, when Moana 2 contributed $225.44M.

data.title: Goldman watching for 3 conditions that could support a stock correction bottom
data.description:
Goldman Sachs is watching for three potential catalysts that could signal a bottom in the current equity correction and set the stage for a market recovery.

The S&P 500 (SPY) (IVV) (VOO) has fallen 12% from its Oct. 6 record high, exceeding the median 10% calendar-year peak-to-trough decline seen since 1980. The Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) has dropped 20%. Historically, following 22 S&P 500 corrections of at least 10% since 1980, the index gained an average 4% over the next three months, rising in 73% of those episodes.

Goldman said the first condition it is watching for is news that increases investor confidence in the outlook for earnings tied to AI investment and monetization. 

The second would be an improvement in the macro backdrop, including a dovish signal from the Federal Reserve. 

The third would be a significant further decline in investor positioning, a feature that has often accompanied previous market bottoms.

That last condition has not yet been met broadly. Hedge funds have sold heavily in recent weeks, with net leverage dropping to its lowest level since April 2025, but Goldman’s broader measure of equity positioning remains above average.

The firm’s U.S. Equity Sentiment Indicator, which combines nine measures of positioning across institutional, retail and foreign investors, stood at 0.7 as of Nov. 20. Meanwhile, U.S. equity mutual funds and ETFs have attracted nearly $170B of inflows since the start of Q4, while asset-manager equity futures positioning ranks in the 82nd percentile of the past decade.

The selloff has also broadened beyond AI. Goldman’s AI basket has fallen 32% since Oct. 6, while the S&P 500 excluding AI is now 6% below its high, and cyclical stocks have begun underperforming defensives as investors mark down expectations for economic growth.

Despite the correction, Goldman still forecasts the S&P 500 reaching 8,700 over the next 12 months.

data.title: SA Asks: How much of a threat is Anthropic's multi-chip strategy to Nvidia?
data.description:
How much of a threat is Anthropic's (ANT) multi-chip strategy, which allows its AI agents to run on multiple chip families, to Nvidia's dominance in the industry?

Seeking Alpha analysts The Techie, Victor Dergunov, Danil Sereda, and Bashar Issa weigh in. 

The Techie: While I think Anthropic’s (ANT) multi-chip strategy poses risks to Nvidia’s (NVDA) market share, I wouldn’t say it’s exactly existential to the company. As of now, six out of seven Nvidia customers are building or using custom chips, so I think the industry is already moving away, and things will get worse in 2027. We know that the frontiers will make up 15% of Nvidia’s revenue this year, and while I don’t expect that figure to decline next year, I have a hard time seeing it grow.

Victor Dergunov: I believe Anthropic's (ANT) multi-chip strategy illustrates that other major chip players exist, such as Broadcom (AVGO), Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and others. However, I don't believe this dynamic implies insufficient demand or that demand for Nvidia (NVDA) chips will likely decline in the near to intermediate term. 

Danil Sereda: Anthropic (ANT) is doing it right by hedging chip supplies, just like any big company does nowadays. It doesn't look like an existential threat to Nvidia’s dominance, in my understanding. Weekly token volume is surging rapidly, the whole AI market is expanding, and so are Anthropic's operations. It already scaled to an $81B annualized revenue run rate ahead of its IPO. 

It's good to see them experimenting with custom silicon like Amazon's (AMZN) AWS Trainium and Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Google TPUs. But the demand for massive acceleration in frontier capabilities is making Nvidia the main raw throughput provider. 

In fact, Nvidia's (NVDA) partnership with Anthropic (ANT) has been expanding, with Nvidia broadening Anthropic's access to Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity across cloud providers. On its latest earnings call, Nvidia management stated it expects major frontier labs to contribute around 15% to its data center revenue this year. The Techie, another SA author, calculated next year's figure at 24%.

So, I don't see any abrupt threat to Nvidia (NVDA) because of Anthropic's (ANT) supply hedging strategies. If there were indeed a major risk, we'd already see it in Nvidia's recent earnings revisions. There are no indications of that so far.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)

Bashar Issa: Anthropic’s (ANT) multi-chip strategy is naturally bad for Nvidia (NVDA) in the short term, but potentially good for the AI sector, including Nvidia, in the long run. 

Nvidia (NVDA) needs to lower its prices because, at this stage, data center unit economics are distorted, in large part by high GPU costs. As mentioned in a recent article, Nvidia (NVDA) generates $4 in revenue for every $1 in COGS. These high margins are not sustainable. 

A successful multi-chip strategy might be the catalyst needed to bring some normalization to the sector. That would put pressure on Nvidia's margins in the short term, but healthier data center economics could support more sustainable demand for its GPUs in the long run.

data.title: OpenAI calls for industry-wide AI brake tied to perplexity
data.description:
OpenAI (OPENAI) is calling for frontier AI developers to adopt common limits on model development tied partly to perplexity, arguing that improvements in the metric can foreshadow the emergence of powerful and unpredictable new capabilities.

In a post Sunday, OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed an industry standard that would establish measurable thresholds developers agree not to cross until corresponding advances are made in understanding and monitoring AI behavior (AIQ) (ARTY) (THNQ) (BOTZ) (CHAT).

Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token, with lower readings representing better performance. OpenAI generally tracks its logarithm, also known as cross-entropy loss, and Pachocki argued that the measure has remained unusually useful for tracking the underlying intelligence created during pretraining even as downstream AI benchmarks rapidly become obsolete.

OpenAI said GPT-3.5 registered log-perplexity of about 0.99 on its main internal evaluation dataset, while GPT-4 reached about 0.91. As losses moved below 0.8, the company began seeing transformative capabilities in areas including cybersecurity and mathematics. A model at roughly 0.76 began producing what Pachocki described as groundbreaking mathematical results.

Looking ahead, Pachocki said OpenAI expects further transformative capabilities as models move into roughly the 0.68-0.70 range, although the company does not know what those capabilities will be.

That uncertainty underpins the proposed development limits. Pachocki said frontier labs should agree on shared evaluation and red-teaming standards and establish a first threshold they would not cross until monitoring technology reached a defined milestone, such as a successor to current chain-of-thought monitoring systems.

The proposal comes as OpenAI sees AI beginning to contribute to its own development. Pachocki said an acceleration in pretraining research could emerge as soon as 2027 if AI systems begin generating fundamental algorithmic advances, potentially speeding progress faster than alignment and monitoring techniques can keep pace.

OpenAI acknowledged that perplexity is an imperfect common standard. Results can be difficult to compare between laboratories because developers use different datasets and training mixtures, and perplexity does not capture all capability gains, including those produced by chain-of-thought reasoning.

Still, Pachocki argued that greater transparency around the measure could provide the industry with a shared scientific basis for pacing increasingly capable AI systems.

data.title: Delta flights delayed due to automated system issue
data.description:
Delta Air Lines (DAL) flights traveling to and from Atlanta have been delayed following a problem with the system that calculates a plane’s weight and balance, the FAA said, according to multiple reports.

According to an FAA advisory, flights have been delayed for about an hour. The delay affects all Delta flights departing to Atlanta from within the contiguous United States, as well as flights leaving Atlanta. Delta is the only commercial airline currently subject to the delay program.

The issue centers on the system that calculates the total weight of an airplane—including its airframe, fuel, passengers, and baggage. This system also helps pilots determine the plane’s center of gravity and proper weight distribution—key data points for flight safety.

In a statement on Sunday, Delta said its teams are using manual workarounds to safely depart flights while efforts continue to restore automation. The airline also noted it is coordinating with air traffic controllers to help reduce congestion at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, Delta’s largest hub.

data.title: DNI Clayton says U.S. probing alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang.
data.description:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton declined Sunday to say whether Alice Huang, the woman reportedly involved in an affair with former Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang, passed information to the Chinese government or otherwise assisted Beijing.

Asked directly on ABC’s This Week whether Huang had helped the Chinese Communist government, Clayton said Attorney General Blanche had made clear that “there is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her,” adding that he would await its outcome.

Clayton also did not say with confidence that Nvidia chips had not been used to support the Chinese military. Instead, he called Nvidia’s chips “the jewel” of advanced technology and said people have broken the law to obtain access to them, pointing to existing indictments involving other companies. He said the issue underscored the importance of controlling access to the most advanced U.S. technology while allowing less-sensitive technology to support global infrastructure development.

Clayton also said he did not know Alice Huang’s current whereabouts after host Jonathan Karl noted reports that she was in China.

The comments came amid broader scrutiny of U.S. controls on advanced AI chips. Sen. Tom Cotton has accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of ignoring warnings about Chinese front companies and allowing damage to U.S. national security, an allegation Clayton declined to address directly.

data.title: Global equities suffer weekly losses amid AI rout, inflation worries
data.description:
US stock indexes ended the week lower as Anthropic’s (ANT) IPO failed to revive sentiment towards AI-related stocks. Concerns resurfaced over whether the returns would justify the enormous sums being invested and borrowed to finance the AI boom

Nvidia (NVDA) reported another beat-and-raise quarter but shares lost more than 45% of its value since its peak in early October, still pressured by tighter export controls on its chips and uncertainty with its new leadership.

Meanwhile, Federal Reserve officials broadly signalled that further interest rate hikes would likely be needed to bring inflation back to the central bank’s target, according to the October FOMC minutes.

For the week, the S&P 500 (SP500) and Nasdaq (COMP:IND) slumped 8% and 10%.

Across the Atlantic, the European equities (STOXX) ended the week 5.7% lower.

The European Commission upgraded its 2026 Eurozone growth outlook to 1.2%, up from 0.9%, citing a stronger economic outlook than previously anticipated.

On the data front, eurozone inflation accelerated to its highest level in over three years, reaching twice the ECB’s target.

UK retail sales rebounded in October, outperforming expectations, while inflation edged higher to its highest level in a year, though remaining below forecasts.

In the week, London’s FTSE 100 (UKX) equities fell over 4%, its worst performance since the outbreak of the Iran war, while Germany (DAX:IND) and France (CAC:IND) markets slipped 7.1% and 5%, respectively.

Major corporate news from Europe this week:

  • Deutsche Bank (DB) internal documents indicated that the bank processed $582M of suspicious payments linked to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, who died in 2019.

The Asia-Pacific markets 

The People's Bank of China left its key lending rates unchanged at record lows for the 18th consecutive month, holding the one-year LPR at 3.0% and the five-year LPR at 3.5%.

China’s economic growth weakened in October as retail sales, industrial output and investment missed expectations.

In the last week, Chinese markets (SHCOMP) lost 2.8%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 (NKY:IND) fell nearly 8 as the unwinding of the artificial intelligence trade intensified%.

Japan’s economy unexpectedly contracted in the third quarter, ending its growth streak as weak consumer spending weighed on activity, while inflation accelerated to its highest level in nearly a year.

data.title: Notable healthcare headlines for the week: Health insurers, Pfizer, and J&J in focus
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages plummeted lower on Friday and finished deep in the red as the tech selloff intensified.

The blue-chip Dow closed 1.9% lower, the benchmark S&P 500 slipped 3.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite tumbled 5.2%.

The S&P 500 Health Care Sector Index (XLV) tumbled more than 6% for the week.

The top S&P 500 healthcare gainers and losers for the past week are as follows:

Top gainers:

Stryker (SYK) +0.12%

Top five losers:

UnitedHealth Group (UNH) -16.59%

Humana (HUM) -13.33%

Moderna (MRNA) -12.65%

Insulet (PODD) -12.64%

Veeva Systems (VEEV) -11.71%

Here are some of the important healthcare stories from this week:

Health insurers extend slide amid ‘Medicare for All’ push

Managed care firms fell for the third straight session on Thursday after Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to become the next House speaker, outlined his health care agenda, which some progressive Democrats viewed as a stepping stone for a sweeping “Medicare for All” health program.

After winning House Democrats' nomination to become Speaker of the House on Wednesday, the New York congressman pledged to lower Medicare eligibility age, expand coverage to every child, and expand benefits to areas like dental and hearing, which traditional Medicare does not cover.

“That is a really important step towards Medicare for All,” Politico reported, quoting Rep. Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.), who has led Medicare for All legislation and is a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

M4A represents a risk to health insurers given its potential to replace most or all private insurance with a publicly funded single-payer national health insurance program that guarantees coverage for Americans.

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), who is expected to become the chairman of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee in January when Democrats take control of the Senate, welcomed Jeffries' remarks.

Sanders, who currently serves as the ranking member on the HELP committee, told MS NOW he was “very glad” to see Jeffries’ plan. “Jeffries basically supported the first year of Medicare for All,” Sanders added in a separate interview with The Associated Press.

Managed care stocks are also under pressure after the Trump administration on Monday announced plans to crack down on fraud and waste in federal and state-sponsored health programs in a move that could particularly impact Medicare Advantage insurers, according to TD Cowen.

The proposed rule, titled the Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare (CRUSH), “creates a potentially material, although likely protracted and litigated, exposure for MA insurers,” wrote analyst Ryan Langston.

Listed managed care firms: UnitedHealth (UNH), Humana (HUM), Centene (CNC), Cigna (CI), CVS Health (CVS), Elevance Health (ELV), Molina Healthcare (MOH), Clover Health (CLOV), Alignment Healthcare (ALHC), and Oscar Health (OSCR)

J&J in discussions to buy Ollin Biosciences for up to $3.4B - report

Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) is in talks to acquire privately held biotech company Ollin Biosciences for up to $3.4B, with a deal potentially being announced as soon as Monday, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The proposed deal includes an upfront cash payment of $2.2B to Ollin's investors, with another $1.2B potentially payable upon meeting specified development and commercial milestones. An agreement could be announced as soon as Monday, although the discussions remain ongoing and the transaction is not yet certain, the report added.

The acquisition would expand Johnson & Johnson's (JNJ) exposure to retinal disease treatments, complementing its existing contact lens business.

Eli Lilly to acquire Calytrix Bio in up to $1.5B deal

Eli Lilly (LLY) acquired privately held Calytrix Bio in a deal that could be worth up to $1.5B to the biotech focused on rare blood disorder treatments.

Calytrix will receive an unspecified upfront payment. The $1.5B value is based on that amount as well as achieving clinical and regulatory milestones.

Novartis drops after updating mid-term outlook

Novartis (NVS) shares fell in Zurich on Thursday after the Swiss drugmaker updated its mid-term guidance, indicating a 5% compound annual growth rate for net sales from 2026 to 2031 on a forex-adjusted basis.

The revised outlook fell short of the 5% - 6% forex-adjusted CAGR the company projected last year for 2025- 2030 and followed several trial setbacks the Basel, Switzerland-based company faced recently.

However, the company raised peak sales guidance for several key brands, including multiple sclerosis therapy Kesimpta and cholesterol drug Leqvio, which are now projected to generate $6B - $8B and $4B - $5B in peak sales, respectively. The company said it is on track to return to the previously targeted over 40% core operating income margin by 2029.

Pfizer, Starna ink cell therapy licensing deal worth up to $2.6B

Pfizer (PFE) on Wednesday announced an exclusive licensing agreement with China-based RNA medicines company Starna Therapeutics to develop and commercialize chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies as part of a deal worth up to $2.6B.

Under the agreement, the New York-based pharma giant will pay $330M upfront to Starna and receive ex-China rights to develop, manufacture, and commercialize preclinical CAR-T programs targeting autoimmune diseases.

Additionally, the Jiangsu-based biotech is entitled to receive up to $2.3B in milestone payments as well as royalties based on net sales of commercialized products.

Pfizer (PFE) will also receive rights to use Starna’s in vivo CAR-T technology in inflammation, immunology, and oncology, as well as options to exclusively license compounds created under a separate research collaboration.

Another option will give the COVID-19 vaccine maker the right to expand its territory to include exclusive rights in Greater China for licensed compounds and products
